French philosopher whose work explores multiplicity, becoming, and the creation of concepts. These notes concern his reading of Nietzsche.
forces.
See also: action theory and Nietzsche.
In Nietzsche and Philosophy, Deleuze treats will to power as the principle determining relations between forces. Calling it another force obscures that distinction. A desire for domination already presupposes a valuation of power.1
Active and reactive name qualities of forces: active forces create forms and directions, while reactive forces conserve and adapt. Affirmation and negation name qualities of the will to power. These pairs are related and must be kept distinct.1
In his reading of Nietzsche’s genealogy of morals, overcoming nihilism requires a change in how values are produced. Negation becomes subordinate to affirmation; opposition to existing values alone leaves that source of evaluation unexamined.1
His account of multiplicity asks how something acquires consistency while its relations change. Tampio distinguishes countable multiplicities from qualitative ones, such as a changing mood. The two can coexist in the same experience.2
Deleuze reads the dice throw as an affirmation of becoming. Throwing affirms chance, including its multiplicity and chaos; the combination formed when the dice land affirms necessity. Both moments belong to the same throw. This is his philosophical reading of eternal return.31
